motions.text: That the Traffic Calming Policy Update (2026), included as Attachment 1 to report 2026-129, titled "Traffic Calming Policy Update" dated April 7, 2026, be approved.

motions.text_html: 1. That the use of speed cushions be removed from the Traffic Calming Policy, included as Attachment-1 to report 2026-129.

motions.name: Amendment to the First Amendment of the Main Motion
motions.text: That the use of speed cushions be used as a last resort only within the Traffic Calming Policy, included as Attachment-1 to report 2026-129.
motions.text_html: 1. That the use of speed cushions be used as a last resort only within the Traffic Calming Policy, included as Attachment-1 to report 2026-129.
motions.post_html: The motion was ruled out of order by the Chair as it was contrary to the Main Motion.

motions.name: First Amendment to the Main Motion
motions.text: That the use of speed cushions be removed from the Traffic Calming Policy, included as Attachment-1 to report 2026-129.
motions.text_html: 1. That the use of speed cushions be removed from the Traffic Calming Policy, included as Attachment-1 to report 2026-129.

motions.name: Second Amendment to Main Motion
motions.text: That staff be directed to remove existing speed cushions from bike lanes, subject to $60,000 being added for this purpose through the 2027 budget confirmation process to allow this work to be completed without impacting other planned traffic calming work as outlined in the Traffic Calming Policy; and. That City Council respectfully requests that the Mayor add $60,000 to the 2027 capital budget, funded by the tax levy, to remove speed cushions from bike lanes. That Staff be directed to review alternative methods of protecting against driver behaviour in areas where speed cushions and bike lanes coexist throughout 2026, and provide a report back to Council in advance of the 2027 budget confirmation process with options and estimated costs for consideration.
motions.text_html:
1. That staff be directed to remove existing speed cushions from bike lanes, subject to $60,000 being added for this purpose through the 2027 budget confirmation process to allow this work to be completed without impacting other planned traffic calming work as outlined in the Traffic Calming Policy; and.
  2. That City Council respectfully requests that the Mayor add $60,000 to the 2027 capital budget, funded by the tax levy, to remove speed cushions from bike lanes.
  3. That Staff be directed to review alternative methods of protecting against driver behaviour in areas where speed cushions and bike lanes coexist throughout 2026, and provide a report back to Council in advance of the 2027 budget confirmation process with options and estimated costs for consideration.
motions.post_html: This motion was withdrawn by the mover and seconder.

motions.name: Third Amendment to Main Motion
motions.text: That staff be directed to maintain an active, internal tracking registry of the approximately 200 streets that were previously scheduled for review under traffic calming, but do not qualify for the 25 prioritized locations under the updated 2026 Traffic Calming Policy. And that staff be directed to formally review these registered streets for alternative Vision Zero safety measures (such as seasonal flex posts, speed radar boards, leading pedestrian intervals, etc.), and report back to Council annually via public facing communication, detailing which alternative measures have been deployed to address speeding and volume concerns.
motions.text_html: 1. That staff be directed to maintain an active, internal tracking registry of the approximately 200 streets that were previously scheduled for review under traffic calming, but do not qualify for the 25 prioritized locations under the updated 2026 Traffic Calming Policy. And that staff be directed to formally review these registered streets for alternative Vision Zero safety measures (such as seasonal flex posts, speed radar boards, leading pedestrian intervals, etc.), and report back to Council annually via public facing communication, detailing which alternative measures have been deployed to address speeding and volume concerns.
motions.post_html: Council recessed (7:21 p.m.) Council reconvened (7:23 p.m.). Councillor Downer raised a Point of Order regarding the use of temporary speed cushions for construction detour mitigation. Mayor Guthrie encouraged discussion to continue.

motions.name: Main Motion, as Amended
motions.text: That the Traffic Calming Policy Update (2026), included as Attachment 1 to report 2026-129, titled "Traffic Calming Policy Update" dated April 7, 2026, be approved, as amended. That staff be directed to maintain an active, internal tracking registry of the approximately 200 streets that were previously scheduled for review under traffic calming, but do not qualify for the 25 prioritized locations under the updated 2026 Traffic Calming Policy. And that staff be directed to formally review these registered streets for alternative Vision Zero safety measures (such as seasonal flex posts, speed radar boards, leading pedestrian intervals, etc.), and report back to Council annually via public facing communication, detailing which alternative measures have been deployed to address speeding and volume concerns.
motions.text_html:
1. That the Traffic Calming Policy Update (2026), included as Attachment 1 to report 2026-129, titled "Traffic Calming Policy Update" dated April 7, 2026, be approved, as amended.
  2. That staff be directed to maintain an active, internal tracking registry of the approximately 200 streets that were previously scheduled for review under traffic calming, but do not qualify for the 25 prioritized locations under the updated 2026 Traffic Calming Policy. And that staff be directed to formally review these registered streets for alternative Vision Zero safety measures (such as seasonal flex posts, speed radar boards, leading pedestrian intervals, etc.), and report back to Council annually via public facing communication, detailing which alternative measures have been deployed to address speeding and volume concerns.

motions.item_title: Support for Canadian Chinese Heritage Month
motions.text: That Guelph City Council supports United Against Hate Canada and the Guelph Chinese Canadian Cultural Group in their call to the Federal Government to champion a motion to create and recognize an annual Canadian Chinese Heritage Month; and That a copy of this resolution be sent to the Right Honourable Mark Carney, Prime Minister of Canada; the Honourable Marc Miller, Minister of Canadian Identity and Culture; Dominique O’Rourke, MP for Guelph; and Michael Chong, MP for Wellington—Halton Hills.
motions.text_html:
1. That Guelph City Council supports United Against Hate Canada and the Guelph Chinese Canadian Cultural Group in their call to the Federal Government to champion a motion to create and recognize an annual Canadian Chinese Heritage Month; and
  2. That a copy of this resolution be sent to the Right Honourable Mark Carney, Prime Minister of Canada; the Honourable Marc Miller, Minister of Canadian Identity and Culture; Dominique O’Rourke, MP for Guelph; and Michael Chong, MP for Wellington—Halton Hills.
